Evidence objective: Screen a soluble, non-polymeric component for ready biodegradability
Appropriate method class: OECD TG 301, with method selected for solubility, volatility, adsorption, and test substance form
Boundary: Standardized laboratory screening in defined mineral medium. oecd

Evidence objective: Assess polymeric component behavior in aerobic aqueous conditions
Appropriate method class: ISO 14851 oxygen-demand measurement and/or ISO 14852 CO2CO_2CO2​-evolution measurement
Boundary: Laboratory test of a documented polymer specimen, inoculum, temperature, and duration. pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih

Evidence objective: Test biodegradation potential under high or variable salinity
Appropriate method class: Salinity-conditioned aquatic microcosm using representative canal inoculum and a documented adaptation of a relevant standard method; OECD 306 may inform saline-water endpoint design but was developed for seawater conditions
Boundary: A Phoenix canal is not seawater, and salinity variation must be explicitly reproduced and reported. aropha

Evidence objective: Measure field conditions affecting degradation or material release
Appropriate method class: Temperature, conductivity/salinity proxy, dissolved oxygen, pH, oxidation-reduction potential, flow, turbidity, water level
Boundary: Sensors require calibration, QA/QC, drift checks, and data-quality flags.

Appropriate method class: Oxygen uptake, CO2CO_2CO2​ evolution, DOC removal under a controlled protocol
Can in-situ sensors satisfy it?: Partially, but not as a replacement
Boundary: Sensors may record DO or CO2CO_2CO2​ in a controlled apparatus; laboratory controls, blanks, inoculum checks, and analytical method remain required. oecd+1

Evidence objective: Quantify PFAS in water and sediment
Appropriate method class: Validated targeted laboratory analysis such as EPA method families chosen for the matrix and analytes
Boundary: Field sensors do not presently replace validated PFAS analyte-specific laboratory measurements for defensible concentration reporting. epa+1

Appropriate method class: Laboratory CEC procedure, such as sodium-acetate or ammonium displacement methods
Boundary: CEC is a sediment/soil property requiring controlled extraction and analysis. epa+1

Appropriate method class: Standardized laboratory analysis with controlled sample handling
Boundary: Proxy sensing may support operations, but it does not replace the reference result.
